Pajusaṇaadhikamāsavicāra
Jain. BP. p. 204b.
See Paryuṣaṇāº.

Pajoka
poet. Skm. p. 212 (Lahore edn.); verse 1552 (Calcutta edn.).

Pajjamadhu
or Padyamadhu. Pāli. 104 stanzas in praise of Buddha. by Buddhappiya, pupil of Ānanda; composed probably in 1300 A. D.
Colombo p. 57 (2 mss.). Colombo D. I. 1272. [Page007-b]
Pt.. (1) by Edmund R. Goonaratna, JPTS. 1887, p.. 1-16. (2) by D. G. Koparkar, Ahmednagar College Publications. Ahmednagar, 1953.

Pajjuṇṇakahā
or pradyumnakathA Jain. Pkt. in 15 sandhis; first 8 sandhis by Sim3ha, son of Pampāi an. the rest by Mahākavi Sim3ha of Gujarat, son of Budha Rālhaṇa an. Jinamatī; composed before Sam3. 1208 a. Bambhaṇavāḍā near Sirohi.
See Jaina Sid. Bhās. XX. ii. p. 27; also Jainism in Rajasthan p. 161.

Pajjunna(pradyumna)
Jain. preceptor of Jinadāsagaṇi Mahattara (a. of Niśīthasūtrāvacūrṇi. BORI. D. XVII. ii. 443).

Pajjusaṇādhikāra
Jain. BP. p. 212b.
See Paryuṣaṇādhikāra.
